note: Maison means both house and home; omitting 'home' is a significant learner gap.
Voilà is a presentative expression, not a preposition. It introduces or points out something: 'there is/are; there/here it is'.
proposed_english: there is/are; there it is; here it is; there you are

note: The unlabelled derogatory/dated sense in the current gloss is inappropriate as a core beginner definition. The central meanings are girl and daughter.
proposed_english: girl; daughter; female child; young woman (context-dependent)

note: Sentir centrally means to feel and to smell; the existing gloss obscures the basic 'smell' sense and overstates 'taste'.
proposed_english: to feel; to smell; to smell of; to sense

note: French moment means moment/time/while; in physics it can mean moment/torque. English 'momentum' is not the ordinary equivalent.
proposed_english: moment; point in time; a while; moment/torque (physics)

note: The current gloss omits core uses of rendre: give/return something, make someone/something a state, and render/yield. 'Call on' is only through constructions such as rendre visite.
proposed_english: to return; to give back; to make; to render; to yield; to visit (rendre visite)

note: Bonjour does not mean 'goodbye' in standard learner French. The surname entry is irrelevant here.
Moins principally means less/fewer and can mean minus; the current gloss gives only 'minus'.
Plaire is the verb 'to please; to be pleasing; to appeal to', not the English politeness word 'please'.
proposed_english: to please; to be pleasing to; to appeal to

note: For learners, rentrer should foreground return/go home/go back in, with fit/enter and scoring as context-dependent extensions.
proposed_english: to return; to go/come home; to go back in; to re-enter; to fit; to score (context-dependent)

note: The current entry omits the literal core noun 'air' and gives an unclear 'air (pretension)' gloss.
proposed_english: air; appearance; look; manner; tune; aria

note: Mort is both the noun 'death/dead person' and the adjective/past participle 'dead'; the current meaning lists only death.
Tenir centrally means hold/keep; 'behave' is construction-dependent. The basic 'hold' sense should be explicit.
proposed_english: to hold; to keep; to maintain; to hold on; to care about/be attached to (tenir à)

note: Affaire centrally means matter/business/affair/case; the current gloss omits the common business/matter readings.
proposed_english: matter; business; affair; case; deal; thing (context-dependent)

note: The current gloss foregrounds the dated/slang 'pimp' sense. For learner French, mec should primarily be guy/man/dude and can mean boyfriend in context.
Devenir as a verb means 'to become'; 'to come from' is venir de, not devenir. The noun le devenir can mean future/development/fate.
